The $27.6B still available under the ATM is NOT modelled as future dilution: an issue at market price is value-neutral per share and the cash would land in the bridge; if it is drawn below IV it is mildly dilutive (~97M shares at the current price, 0.8%).

The CSV's CashAndEquivalents + ShortTermInvestments = 265,098 also contains 90,384 of marketable EQUITY securities (Level 1), carved out here and carried in equity_bridge at a haircut. total_debt = long-term debt 125,102 + current portion/CP 1,016 (CSV TotalDebt, Q3 2026); finance lease liabilities 3,705 are deducted in equity_bridge. inputs.sbc_source: TTM to 2026-09-30. SBC = share-settled cash-flow add-back: FY2025 24,953 - 9M 2025 17,882 + 9M 2026 23,338 = 30,409 (6.5% of TTM revenue). Equity-award taxes = 'Net payments related to stock-based award activities' (financing): FY2025 14,167 - 9M 2025 9,001 + 9M 2026 17,424 = 22,590. Alphabet publishes no combined adjusted-EBITDA figure, so the two lines are summed per the method (52,999 = 11.2% of revenue). The settlement line is inflated by the ~3x share-price rise over the vesting window; the FORWARD sbc_pct_path is therefore anchored at 8.0% (6.5% grant-date expense + ~1.5pp for the expected vest-date excess at the modelled cost of equity), not at 11.2%, which would assume the stock keeps tripling every three years. Cash-settled awards (kpis StockBasedCompTotal) are already inside OCF and are not added. Interest income = FY2025 4,337 - 9M 2025 3,128 + 9M 2026 4,579 = 5,788, stripped because the cash pile is added back in the bridge.

ttm_anchors_2026Q3.note: D&A = depreciation (FY2025 21,136 - 9M25 15,096 + 9M26 21,955 = 27,995) + intangible amortisation (~1,050 incl. Wiz). Operating income includes ~$3.1B of EU DMA and PriceRunner charges, left in as recurring.

inputs.wacc_rationale: USD flows, USD discount rate. 10-yr UST ~4.2% + beta ~1.0 x ERP ~5% = ~9.2% cost of equity; $126B of debt at ~4.5% pre-tax is ~3.5% of a $3.5T capital base, so WACC rounds to 9%. Single 9% across all three scenarios: scenario risk is carried in the driver paths and the probability weights, not in a per-scenario premium (charge risk once). The prior June model used 8/9/12; its 12% bear rate applied to three years of negative FCF produced a $33 bear IV that was an artefact, not a finding.
inputs.lease_treatment: Operating leases (liabilities 20,508; cost ~$3.7B/yr) stay inside EBITDA as rent under US GAAP -- treatment A; lease liabilities are NOT in net debt. Finance leases (liabilities 3,705; amortisation inside D&A, principal in financing) are deducted in equity_bridge. $130.5B of data-centre/energy leases not yet commenced (2026-2031) will raise operating lease cost by an estimated 1-2pp of revenue by 2030; the EBITDA margin path is held at 49% rather than higher partly to absorb that.
inputs.nci_treatment: Waymo and the other Other Bets are consolidated and loss-making (Q3 2026 segment operating loss $2.05B) and sit inside the flows; no NCI deduction and no separate Waymo value. The February 2026 Series D ($16B at $126B) implies ~$95-100B for Alphabet's majority stake (~$8/share) -- unmodelled upside, offset by the un-separated burn. Crux AI (Blackstone JV, equity-method, up to $10B backstop; $75.7B of data-centre financial-support obligations in total) is off balance sheet; its risk is carried through the bear capex path, not the bridge.
inputs.notes: MODEL: owner-FCF component DCF (dcf-methods routing: operating company, consumer internet / cloud; US filer, so the non-US adaptations do not apply beyond the matching-asset rule for the securities). Prior June 2026 DCF was a hand-built 'OCF growth minus explicit capex' model with no SBC charge; this is a methodology change to the house engine, reconciled below. KEY JUDGMENT -- normalised vs capex-depressed FCF: the engine does not normalise capex away; it models the cycle explicitly. Capex is ~$200B in FY2026 (guided, 9M actual 132.0) and ~$300B in FY2027 (reported from the Oct-28 call, not in filing text), so owner FCF is negative in FY2027-FY2029 in every scenario and the value is almost entirely the FY2030+ recovery as capex intensity falls from ~50% of revenue toward 17% and D&A rises from 6% to ~16-18%. D&A only touches the tax line in the engine (it is added back), so the IV is driven by the capex % path, the revenue path and the EBITDA margin. Cash tax starts at 8% (100% bonus depreciation on $300B/yr of mostly-qualifying equipment) and ramps to 18% by FY2034 -- not perpetuated. Terminal: Gordon binds in base and bear; the 20x cap binds in bull. PRICE: regular close on the day of the -12.6% post-earnings move; not an after-hours print but volatile -- re-check at the next close.

historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: EPS 3yr CAGR (33.3%) diverges >30% from equity 3yr CAGR (17.5%): FY2025 EPS carries large unrealized equity-security gains and 9M 2026 EPS $14.24 carries +$127B of them; FY2024 EPS $8.04 is the cleaner base. Equity 5yr CAGR (13.3%) is lifted by the $84.75B June 2026 raise. Revenue 5yr CAGR (17.2%) is the cleanest anchor.
historical_growth.notes: CAGRs are FY2022->FY2025 (3yr) and FY2020->FY2025 (5yr). Owner-FCF CAGR (0.7% / 6.0%) is far below reported FCF CAGR (6.9% / 11.3%): SBC + net-share-settlement taxes grew from 18.7B (FY2020) to 39.1B (FY2025), so an increasing share of reported cash growth was paid for in stock. The owner-FCF series: FY2020 22.3B, FY2021 40.0B, FY2022 29.2B, FY2023 33.3B, FY2024 33.3B, FY2025 29.8B, TTM Q3-2026 -39.0B. The history is not the forward anchor; the component build is.

base.growth_rationale: FY2027 +21%: Cloud ~+50% (backlog $560.8B, 55% converting inside 24 months = ~$150B/yr, plus first full year of external TPU system sales) on Services +9% (Search +9-10% after the Q3 2026 deceleration to +12%, YouTube +9%, subs/devices +10%, Network flat). Decelerates 17/14/11 as Cloud laps the backlog surge, then 9->4% as the business matures into a ~$1.3T revenue company by FY2036 (10-yr CAGR 10.1% vs 18.6% for the past ten).
base.capex_rationale: Dollars: FY2027 ~$300B (reported guidance), FY2028 $320B, FY2029 $310B, FY2030 $295B, then $275/255/240/230/225/222B -- i.e. the build plateaus in 2028-29 and only declines slowly in dollars; the % falls because revenue grows into it. $924B of purchase commitments through 2031 support a ~$250-320B/yr run-rate. Terminal 17% of revenue vs 9-10% pre-2024: a permanently more capital-intensive, cloud-heavy mix (Cloud ~45% of revenue at ~30% intensity + Services at ~5%).
base.da_rationale: Depreciation 9M 2026 21,955 (+45% YoY) on a 6-yr server / 25-yr building book; ~$1.4T of capex 2026-2030 lifts D&A from 6.4% of revenue to ~18% by FY2030-31, then settles just below terminal capex (16% vs 17%) consistent with 3.5-4% growth. Affects only the cash-tax line in the engine.
base.margin_rationale: TTM pre-SBC EBITDA margin 45.9% (46.6% ex ~$3.1B of EU fines/damages). Cloud mix shift (36% segment OI margin in Q2 2026 and rising, i.e. 50%+ EBITDA) and opex leverage (headcount +8% vs revenue +25%) lift it to 49% by FY2032; held there to absorb rising operating-lease cost from the $130.5B of not-yet-commenced leases, Alphabet-level AI R&D (+100% YoY) and lower-margin TPU hardware sales.
base.tax_rationale: Cash taxes paid FY2025 21,526 (~13.5% of pre-tax) vs 16.8% GAAP ETR. 100% bonus depreciation on $300B/yr of mostly-qualifying equipment pushes the cash rate toward single digits in FY2027-28; it ramps to 18% by FY2034 (above the 16.8% ETR, as the accelerated deductions reverse and OECD Pillar 2 bites). Not perpetuated.

bull.rationale: Same ~$300B FY2027 capex in dollars but revenue grows into it faster: Cloud sustains 60%+ into FY2028 as backlog converts and external TPU sales reach the ~$75B BofA models for 2027; ads inside AI Overviews/AI Mode re-accelerate Search to low-teens; Gemini's 1B users and the Apple/Siri deal hold distribution. EBITDA margin to 52% on Cloud scale and opex leverage; capex intensity falls to 15% as the build front-runs demand. SBC % declines faster on a larger revenue base. Terminal 4.0% (prior bull). The 20x cap binds.

bear.rationale: AI answer engines cannibalise Search: Search growth goes from +12% to flat by FY2029 while TAC and AI-serving cost stay; Cloud slows to +25-30% as capacity delays (Crux AI sites) and price competition bite and TPU sales disappoint; FY2027 capex still lands near $300B because the $924B of commitments is locked, then is cut hard. EBITDA margin erodes to 43.5%; terminal operating margin ~19% vs 33% today. Search antitrust data-sharing and EU fines recur. Terminal 2.5% (prior bear). Owner FCF is negative for three years and the terminal FCF margin is only ~15%.

scenario_narratives.base: Alphabet is spending ~$500B over FY2026-27 to turn a $560B Cloud backlog and a 1B-user Gemini franchise into a second core business while Search decelerates from high-teens to high-single-digit growth. Owner FCF is negative through FY2029; the value is the FY2030+ recovery as capex intensity halves and the installed base earns at ~49% EBITDA margins. At a 9% WACC that is worth materially less than the pre-October market price, which was paying for a faster Search re-acceleration and a quicker capex peak.
scenario_narratives.bull: The capex is demand-led: Cloud compounds 60%+ for two more years on backlog plus external TPU systems, AI-Overview ads re-accelerate Search, margins reach 52% and intensity falls to 15% -- Alphabet becomes a ~$1.6T revenue company by FY2036 and the exit multiple cap binds.
scenario_narratives.bear: The Q3 2026 Search deceleration is the start of AI substitution of the core franchise; Cloud growth halves as supply and competition catch up; $300B of FY2027 capex is committed into a market that does not need it, and the business settles at 43% EBITDA margins, 3% growth and a 15% FCF margin -- three years of negative FCF followed by a mature-utility profile.

probability_weighted.weights_rationale: Unchanged from the June 2026 model (25/50/25 vs house default 15/50/35). Bear held at 25% because the Search cannibalisation risk is now in the reported numbers (+12% in Q3 2026 from +19%), the capex ROI is unproven and the regulatory drag recurs; bull held at 25% because it needs Cloud, external TPU sales AND Search AI-ad monetisation all to land together. No going-concern or covenant element -- the bear is a margin and returns story, not solvency.

valuation_philosophy.summary: Owner-FCF component DCF over a 10-year explicit horizon, because the FCF margin is immature in the extreme: capex of ~$200B (FY2026) and ~$300B (FY2027) makes owner FCF negative for roughly three years in every scenario, so a 5-year horizon would capitalise a trough and a flat-margin model would capitalise a one-off. The engine models the cycle rather than normalising it: revenue grows into a capex base that plateaus in dollars, D&A rises to ~17% of revenue and then matches capex at the terminal, and the cash tax rate ramps from bonus-depreciation lows to 18%. SBC and net-share-settlement taxes are expensed and the count is held flat; the equity-securities pile (SpaceX listed, one private AI company unlisted) is brought in at haircuts rather than ignored or taken at mark. The two accounting-regime figures (house vs street) bracket how much of the price depends on treating comp as non-cash.
key_risks_to_valuation: Capex trajectory after FY2027: if ~$300B/yr persists through FY2030 instead of plateauing and falling to 17% of revenue, the FY2030+ FCF recovery slips two years and the base IV falls toward the bear.
Search growth: each 1pp of sustained Search deceleration is ~$3B of near-70%-margin revenue; the bear case is Search flat by FY2029.
Cloud backlog conversion and external TPU sales: the base needs Cloud ~+50% in FY2027; delays at Crux AI sites or supply constraints push it out.
Equity-securities marks: $225B gross (SpaceX listed, one private company) is carried at $120B after haircuts; a 50% move in those marks is ~$5/share.
WACC: 1pp is ~$40-45/share on a valuation that is ~80% terminal value; the market price implies ~7.5-8%.

Financing stack: $19B 6.25% preferred, $27.6B ATM capacity, $75.7B of data-centre backstop obligations and $130.5B of not-yet-commenced leases are all claims or costs that sit outside the flows or bridge in part.
